title: operational-observability-checklist-for-quantized-model-rollouts
content:
Purpose:
A compact, practical checklist for observability (metrics + traces + dashboards + sampling) to accompany rollouts of quantized model variants. Goal is to reduce experiment churn, preserve operator signal fidelity when numeric behavior changes, and bound query costs during early traffic. This doc focuses on small-to-medium rollouts (canary -> 10% -> 50%) for quantized models (int8/4-bit variants) serving tokenized inference paths.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted + dedicated deployments that use the standard serving runtime.
- Quantized variants may expose subtle perf/accuracy tradeoffs; expect different latency percentiles and cache-warmth behavior.
- Operators will have access to tracing and token-level metrics; sampling budgets are limited.
- This is intentionally tactical: advocate for minimal new metrics and use derived dashboards.

High-level observability goals for quantized rollouts:
1) Detect regressions in perceived latency and tail behavior within the first 1 hour of traffic.
2) Surface increased error/hallucination signals tied to quantization artifacts (stability, repetition).
3) Attribute cost changes (tokens/sec, gpu-time-per-token) to model variant.
4) Ensure rollback signal (one metric or score) is available for automated rollback triggers.

Minimum metric set (recommend add only these before canary):
- rollout.variant (tag) -> labelled by model_variant: e.g. model=v1-int8, model=v1-fp16
- request.latency_ms.p50/p90/p99 -> per-variant, route-level
- token.emission_rate_tokens_per_sec -> aggregated by variant and region
- kvcache.hit_rate -> prefix/kv cache warmth, by variant and tenant_cohort
- model.cpu_gpu_ms_per_token -> estimate of compute time per generated token
- output.quality.score -> synthetic eval score computed from internal prompt set (see synthetic probes below)
- error.rate (parse errors, tokenization failures, runtime exceptions) -> by variant

Trace plan (lightweight, canary-friendly):
- Trace anchors: ensure every request includes a trace-id + variant tag.
- Sampling policy: initially sample 100% traces for canary traffic for 10 minutes, then 10% for 2 hours, then 1% for long tail. Rationale: quantized regressions can appear quickly but are rare; front-load coverage.
- Span enrichment: include keys for kvcache_warmth, batch_size, seq_len, and kernel-code-path (e.g., matmul-optimized, fused-attn).
- Trace annotation schema: "variant", "tenant_id_bucket", "probe_synthetic" (true|false).
- Quick trace queries to save as widgets: 1) trace waterfall for high-p99 latency requests; 2) traces filtered where output.quality.score < threshold; 3) span-level breakdown of compute vs serialization.

Synthetic probe design (cheap, fast QA signals):
- Probe set: 30 short prompts representative of main workload slices (e.g., short chat, long-form, code). Keep lightweight to run every minute on canary variant only.
- Metrics from probes: median latency, token delta vs baseline, BLEU/ROUGE similarity to fp16 baseline, hallucination_flag (heuristic), top-k divergence (KL) for logits if available.
- Alerting tier: probe-failure-alert (sev2) triggers if output.quality.score drops > 6 points vs baseline within 15m window.

Dashboard guidance (compact panels to add before canary):
- Single layout canvas with vertical slices: Traffic & rollout, Latency distribution, KV cache warmth, Synthetic probe results, Error breakdown, Cost estimator. Keep to 8-10 panels.
- Panel specifics:
  - Rollout funnel: % traffic by variant over time, success rate by variant
  - Latency heatmap: p50/p90/p99 timelines per variant (stacked small-multiples if many routes)
  - Session-warmth index: per-tenant warmth metric showing cold-start spikes for quantized variant
  - Probe trendline: synthetic score vs baseline with small table of recent failing probes
  - Cost delta gauge: estimate tokens * ms_per_token * price-per-ms (simple formula)
  - Trace-sampled list: recent slow traces with direct link to trace tool and variant tag

Alerting suggestions (keep conservative during canary):
- Sev1 (auto rollback): if output.quality.score drops > 10 points AND p99 latency increases > 2x baseline simultaneously for 5m.
- Sev2: any sustained increase in error.rate > 3x baseline for 10m.
- Sev3: probe failures 30%+ over 30m or probe flakiness correlated to a single kernel_code_path.

Operational runbook snippets (for SRE/Operator):
- Pre-rollout checklist (before shifting traffic):
  1) Confirm variant label propagated to logs and traces.
  2) Confirm synthetic probe scheduled for canary group (smoke run).
  3) Set sampling to 100% for canary for first 10m (temporary override).
  4) Pin monitoring dashboard and enable notifications to oncall.
  5) Confirm cost-estimator tag present to avoid billing surprises.
- During canary (first 60m):
  1) Watch probe score and latency p99; if either breach defined thresholds, pause rollout.
  2) Inspect traces flagged with span attribute kernel_code_path to see if quantized kernel is hotpath.
  3) Check kvcache hit_rate for rapid drops (indicates prefix mismatch due to numeric stability).
- Rollback steps (manual and automated):
  1) Toggle routing policy to previous variant.
  2) Capture trace snapshot and save to incident doc (link to incident template).
  3) Run focused synthetic tests against both variants for regression isolation.

Instrumentation notes (practical tips):
- Avoid adding new high-cardinality tags keyed by full prompt text. Instead use hashed prompt_bucket for attribution.
- Emit model variant as a low-cardinality tag and include an additional boolean for quantization-level (int8,int4).
- For compute_ms_per_token, prefer server-side aggregate metric emitted per batch rather than per-token counters (streamlined cost).

Cost and query-budget controls:
- Create a temporary query-budget allocator for canary (e.g., 5k tokens/min) to prevent runaway probing.
- Ensure dashboard panels include cost delta so PMs can see immediate impact.

Follow-ups and open questions (to resolve pre-canary):
- How to standardize output.quality.score across teams? (proposal: central probe harness and normalized score)
- Should trace retention for canary be extended to 7d for regression hunting? tradeoff with query costs.
- Is there a lightweight way to compute top-k divergence without exposing logits in prod? (noise concerns)

References & links:
- Confluence: quantized-model-onboarding (linked above)
- Jira: ENG-1427 for kernel-path tagging work
- GH PR: serving-runtime instrument-trace-enrichment (#981)

Quick todo (owner: Ava):

Notes to self: keep the checklist lean. If metrics increase signal noise during canary, prefer temporarily increasing sampling and synthetic probe cadence instead of inflating dashboard cardinality.
